Paperlark Privacy Policy

Effective October 9, 2026 · Last updated October 9, 2026

The short version. Your scans, the text recognized in them and your signatures are stored on your iPhone. Text recognition, auto-filing, redaction and AI summaries all run on the device, and nothing is uploaded to us or to any AI service. There is no account and we run no server. Purchases go through Apple. The free version shows ads; the ad companies collect some device data to show them, never your documents, and Pro removes ads entirely.

Who we are

Paperlark is made by an independent developer ("we", "us"). This policy covers the Paperlark iPhone app, its widgets, its Control Center control and its Siri and Shortcuts actions. Questions: SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.

Your documents stay on your device

  • Page images. Each scanned page is saved as a JPEG (the original and the cleaned-up version) in the app's private storage on your iPhone, encrypted at rest with iOS data protection; after a restart the files can't be read until you first unlock your iPhone.
  • Everything else is kept in a local database inside the app: document names and details, the text recognized in your scans, folders and tags, details the app pulls out (such as vendor, dates, amounts and due dates), cached summaries, and signatures and initials you save (stored as drawings).
  • Your settings (such as app lock and Spotlight preferences) are stored on the device too.

There is no iCloud sync in this version, and this data is not kept in the area shared with widgets. We have no server for it and cannot see it. Like any app's data, it is included in your own device backups (iCloud Backup or a computer backup), which Apple and you control.

Processing on your iPhone

  • Text recognition (OCR), including reading barcodes and QR codes, uses Apple's Vision framework on your device.
  • Sorting, naming and filing use on-device keyword rules and Apple's data detectors, and, on iOS 26 devices with Apple Intelligence, Apple's on-device Foundation Models.
  • AI summary and "ask this document" run entirely on your iPhone: with Apple's on-device Foundation Models where available, or a simpler method that picks out key sentences otherwise. They work in Airplane Mode.
  • Smart redaction finds emails, phone numbers, addresses, card numbers, account numbers, Social Security numbers and dates on your device. When you share a redacted copy, black boxes are burned into the page images and the hidden text is removed from the PDF's text layer, so it can't be copied or searched.

Nothing is uploaded to us or to any AI service.

Sharing and exporting

A document leaves Paperlark only when you export it: through the iOS share sheet, Save to Files or Save to Photos. Once you share a document, the app or person you send it to handles it under their own privacy practices. You can protect an exported PDF with a password; Paperlark uses Apple's standard PDF encryption for this, only when you ask.

Spotlight search

So your documents appear when you search on your iPhone, Paperlark adds each document's title, type and recognized text (up to 20,000 characters per document) to the on-device Spotlight index. This index stays on your iPhone. To turn it off, go to Paperlark Settings > Privacy and turn off Find documents in Spotlight; Paperlark then removes its entries. While App Lock is on, iPhone search only shows each document's type, never its name or text.

Widgets

Widgets read a small summary that Paperlark copies into a storage area shared only with its own widgets (an App Group): your document count, up to 4 recent documents and up to 4 documents with a due date coming up, each with its title, type icon, page count, dates, due date and, for bills and receipts, the amount. If you turn off Show titles on widgets, each title is replaced with the document's type (for example "Bill") and no amount is shown. While App Lock is on, widgets show each document's type instead of its title. Widgets never see your page images or recognized text.

Notifications

Notifications are scheduled locally on your iPhone; no notification server is used. Paperlark can remind you 48 hours before a free trial turns into a paid subscription, and of due dates at 9:00 the day before. Bills and invoices with a due date get a reminder the day before by default; switch it off in Settings > Reminders or on the document. You can also turn a reminder on for any other document. With App Lock on, the notification only says 'A bill is due tomorrow.'

Permissions

  • Camera: to scan documents. Camera images are processed on your iPhone and saved only in the app.
  • Face ID (optional app lock): handled entirely by iOS, which also offers your passcode as a fallback. Paperlark only learns whether unlocking succeeded and never receives biometric data.
  • Photos (add only): to save page images to your library. Importing from Photos uses Apple's photo picker, so Paperlark only gets the photos you pick and cannot read the rest of your library.
  • Notifications: see Notifications.
  • App Tracking Transparency: asked only in the free version when ads are switched on, after a short explanation in the app, and never while you are scanning, editing or signing. See Advertising.

Paperlark does not ask for your location, contacts, microphone or calendar.

Files app and opening documents

Paperlark doesn't keep a folder in On My iPhone; use Save to Files to put a copy anywhere you like. You can also open PDFs and images in Paperlark from Files, Mail and other apps; Paperlark copies the file it is given and does not access anything else.

Network connections

Paperlark makes no network connections of its own other than Apple's App Store (prices, purchases, restores and subscription status) and, in the free version, the ad SDKs. Scanning, text recognition, search, summaries, redaction and signing work offline. You can check this yourself in iOS's App Privacy Report (Settings > Privacy & Security > App Privacy Report).

Purchases and subscriptions

Paperlark Pro is sold through Apple's App Store using StoreKit. Apple handles the payment, your payment details, your Apple ID and your billing address. We never see your name, email address or payment information. The app only receives a signed confirmation from Apple saying which product is active (for example, "Yearly, renews on a date" or "Lifetime") so it can unlock Pro and switch off ads. That check happens on your device. Apple's handling of purchase data is covered by Apple's Privacy Policy.

App Store Connect gives us aggregated, non-identifying sales reports (for example, how many trials started in a country). Apple does not give us your identity.

Paperlark Pro is offered as a yearly subscription with a 7-day free trial for eligible new subscribers, and as a one-time lifetime purchase that supports Family Sharing. You can cancel from Paperlark Settings > Manage subscription (which opens Apple's screen) and restore purchases at any time.

Advertising in the free version

The free version of Paperlark shows ads. Buying Paperlark Pro (a subscription or the lifetime purchase) removes all ads, and the ad SDK then stops requesting ads.

Ads are delivered by AppLovin MAX, an ad mediation SDK built into the app. MAX may fill an ad slot from AppLovin itself or from other ad networks it mediates, such as Google AdMob. These companies, not us, receive and process the data described below. We do not receive it in a form that identifies you; we only see aggregated reports such as how many ads were shown and how much they earned.

What the ad SDKs may collect

DataWhenUsed for
Advertising identifier (IDFA)Only if you tap "Allow" on Apple's App Tracking Transparency prompt. If you choose "Ask App Not to Track", iOS gives the SDK an all-zeros identifier instead.Personalized ads, measuring ads across apps (tracking)
Identifier for Vendor (IDFV) and SDK-generated IDsWhenever an ad is requestedFrequency capping, fraud prevention, reporting; not linked across companies' apps without your permission
IP address and approximate (coarse) location derived from itWhenever an ad is requestedDelivering ads, picking the right language/region, legal compliance (for example, privacy rules by region), fraud prevention
Device and app information: device model, iOS version, language, time zone, screen size, network type, carrier, app name and versionWhenever an ad is requestedShowing ads that fit your device, troubleshooting, fraud prevention
Ad interaction data: which ads were shown, taps, video completions, rewarded-ad completionsWhen you see or interact with an adAd delivery, measurement, billing between ad companies, rewarding you for a rewarded ad
Ad SDK diagnostics (crash and performance data about the ad SDK)If the ad SDK has a problemKeeping the ad SDK working

Ad SDKs never get access to your scanned pages, their recognized text, document names, folders, tags, extracted details (such as vendors, amounts and due dates), summaries or signatures. Your documents stay on your iPhone, are never shared with ad partners, and are never used to choose which ads you see. As with any app that shows ads, an ad request does tell the ad network which app it came from (Paperlark).

The app does not request precise location for ads and does not give ad SDKs access to your contacts, camera, microphone or Health data.

Your ad choices

  • App Tracking Transparency (all users). The first time ads might be personalized, the app explains why and then shows Apple's prompt. Choose "Ask App Not to Track" and the ad SDKs cannot use your IDFA or track you across other companies' apps and websites; you will still see ads, but they are non-personalized or based on the content of the app. You can change this at any time in iOS Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking (per app, or turn off "Allow Apps to Request to Track" for every app).
  • In-app consent screen (EEA, UK and Switzerland). In the EEA, the UK and Switzerland, the consent screen opens before ads and can be reopened from Settings > Ad Privacy Choices. It is Google's User Messaging Platform, shown through AppLovin MAX; it asks before any data is used for personalized ads and lets you accept, reject or pick partners and purposes, and change or withdraw your consent later.
  • Remove ads entirely by buying Paperlark Pro. A subscription or lifetime purchase turns off all ads.
  • Limit ad personalization at the partner. Google: My Ad Center.

Ad partners and their privacy policies

  • AppLovin (MAX mediation and AppLovin ads): applovin.com/privacy
  • Google AdMob: Google Privacy Policy and How Google uses information from apps that use its services

We may add or remove mediated ad networks over time. When we add one, we will list it here and update the changelog at the bottom of this page. The full, current list of partners and purposes is also shown in the consent screen where that screen applies.

"Do not sell or share my personal information"

Paperlark Settings > Ad Privacy Choices also has a "Do not sell or share my personal information" switch. When it is on, Paperlark tells AppLovin, and through it the networks it mediates, not to sell or share your personal information for targeted advertising, as US state privacy laws allow. Your choice is stored on your device.

When ads start, and where they appear

  • No ad is requested until you have seen the tracking explanation and, where they apply, Apple's tracking prompt and the consent screen. The ad SDK itself may start just before the consent screen, because that screen is part of it. Google's ad measurement waits until then.
  • The ad SDKs use your IDFA only if you choose "Allow" on Apple's tracking prompt; otherwise they use the identifier for vendor (IDFV) and ads are non-personalized.
  • Banner ads appear only on the documents library list. There is at most one full-screen ad per session, only after an export or share is completed, and never after your first export. Watching a rewarded ad (for example, for a one-time Pro export) is always your choice.
  • Ads never appear in the camera and scanning screens, the editor, signing, redaction, the document assistant, onboarding or the Pro screen.
  • With Pro (subscription or lifetime), no ads are requested. If you buy Pro while ads are running, the ad SDK stops requesting ads at once.
  • If ads are not switched on. Ads run only in versions of the app where ad accounts are configured. In a version without them, no ad SDK starts, no tracking prompt is shown and no data goes to any third party, and the App Store privacy label for that version says so.

We ask our ad partners to block ads for gambling, dating and mature content where their controls allow it. If you see an inappropriate ad in Paperlark, please tell us at SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.

Sensitive documents

People scan IDs, bank statements, medical letters and tax forms. That is why Paperlark keeps them on your iPhone: their images, text and details are never sent to us, never shared with ad partners or anyone else, and never used for advertising, profiling or research. If you use Spotlight, remember that text from your documents can appear in iPhone search results; you can turn that off at any time (see Spotlight search). Use the app lock and redaction for extra protection, and check a redacted copy before you share it.

What we never do

  • No account, sign-in or email address needed.
  • No server holding your documents, no cloud AI or OCR service, and no analytics or crash-reporting SDKs of our own. (Ad SDKs may report their own diagnostics, as described above.)
  • We never sell your data and never use your documents for advertising.
  • This version of Paperlark does not use iCloud sync.

Data retention

  • Documents and their data are kept on your iPhone until you delete them. We keep no copy.
  • Ad data is retained by AppLovin, Google and other ad partners according to their policies linked above.
  • Purchase records are kept by Apple under Apple's policies.
  • Support emails are kept only as long as needed to help you and keep a record of the conversation, then deleted, normally within 24 months. Ask us to delete them sooner at any time.

Deleting your data

  • Delete a document: removes its page files, its Spotlight entries and any reminders for it.
  • Delete everything: Paperlark Settings > Delete everything wipes all documents, files, saved signatures, Spotlight entries and scheduled notifications. It can't be undone.
  • Deleting the app removes all its data. It does not cancel a subscription.
  • Exported copies you saved to Files or Photos or sent to others are outside Paperlark; delete them where you saved them.
  • Ad data: use your ad choices or contact the ad partner; email us and we'll help.

Your privacy rights

Because Paperlark has no account and no server, we do not hold a profile about you. Your app data is on your device, where you can view, export (where the app offers it) and delete it yourself. For data the ad partners collect, you can use the choices above or contact the partner directly. Whatever your location, you can email us and we will help.

EEA, UK and Switzerland (GDPR / UK GDPR)

  • Who is responsible. We, the developer of Paperlark, are the controller for the limited personal data we handle (for example, emails you send us, and the decision to integrate ad SDKs). AppLovin, Google and other ad partners act as independent controllers for the data they collect to deliver and measure ads.
  • Legal bases. Personalized ads and the access to device identifiers they need: your consent, collected through the consent screen and Apple's tracking prompt. Showing non-personalized ads, frequency capping, fraud prevention and security: the legitimate interests of the developer of Paperlark and the ad partners in funding a free app and keeping ads safe. Replying to your support email: our legitimate interest in helping you (or steps you ask for before a contract). Purchases: handled by Apple under Apple's terms.
  • Your rights. Access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection (including to processing based on legitimate interests), data portability, and withdrawing consent at any time without affecting earlier processing. Withdraw ad consent in Paperlark Settings > Ad Privacy Choices; object or ask about anything else by emailing SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD.
  • Complaints. You can complain to your local data protection authority. We would appreciate the chance to fix things first.
  • International transfers. Ad partners may process data in the United States and other countries. They rely on safeguards such as the EU Standard Contractual Clauses and, where they are certified, the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; see their policies above.

California and other US states (CCPA / CPRA and similar laws)

  • Categories collected in the last 12 months (by ad partners through the free version only): identifiers (IDFA with your permission, IDFV, SDK IDs, IP address); internet or other electronic network activity (ad impressions and taps); approximate geolocation derived from IP; device information. Inferences may be drawn by ad partners for personalized ads if you allow it. We do not collect sensitive personal information, and your in-app data is never shared with ad partners.
  • Sources and purposes. Collected directly from your device by the ad SDKs, for the advertising, measurement, security and fraud-prevention purposes described above.
  • "Sale" and "sharing". We do not sell personal information for money. Letting ad partners use identifiers for cross-context behavioral advertising may count as "selling" or "sharing" under California law. To opt out: choose "Ask App Not to Track", and/or open Paperlark Settings > Ad Privacy Choices and opt out of sale/sharing, or email us. You can also buy Pro to remove ads entirely.
  • Your rights. To know/access, delete, correct, opt out of sale or sharing, and limit the use of sensitive personal information (we do not use any). We will not discriminate against you for using these rights; the free version stays the same whether or not you opt out. An authorized agent may make a request on your behalf with your written permission. Because we hold no account data, we may not be able to link ad-partner data to you; we will tell you which partner to contact and how.
  • Retention. See Data retention.
  • Minors. We do not knowingly sell or share the personal information of consumers under 16.

Residents of other US states with consumer privacy laws (for example Virginia, Colorado, Connecticut, Utah, Texas and Oregon) have similar rights to access, delete, correct and opt out of targeted advertising. Use the same steps above or email us. If we decline a request, you can appeal by replying to our answer with "Appeal" in the subject line.

Children

Paperlark is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 (or the minimum age in your country). If you believe a child has provided personal information to us, for example by email, contact us and we will delete it.

Security

Your documents are protected by iOS app sandboxing and are encrypted at rest with iOS data protection (after a restart the files can't be read until you first unlock your iPhone), and you can add a Face ID lock in Paperlark. Because we don't operate a server, there is no developer-held database of your documents that could be breached. Keep your device passcode, your Apple ID and any exported files secure.

Contact

Email SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD for questions, privacy requests or complaints. If you email us, we receive your email address and whatever you write, and use it only to reply. Please never send us your documents or ID numbers. We aim to answer within 7 days, and privacy requests within the time the law requires (30 days under GDPR, 45 days under CCPA).

Changes and changelog

If we change how Paperlark handles data, for example if we add iCloud sync, we will update this page and the date at the top before the change takes effect, and for significant changes we will tell you in the app. The App Store privacy label is kept in line with this page.
